skill.name: Swarm Orchestration
skill.description: Guides multi-agent swarm orchestration with agentic-flow, including topology selection, task routing, shared memory, hooks, and resilience patterns.
skill.summary: Coordinate specialized AI agents through agentic-flow swarm patterns and hooks.
skill.author: ruvnet

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fence backticks in examples. Two command blocks are confirmed medium-risk because they instruct users to run unpinned npx agentic-flow hook commands that execute third-party CLI code locally.

remediation.suggestion: Pin agentic-flow to a reviewed version in every npx example and document package provenance checks before execution.

remediation.issue: Hook commands can change workspace or session state
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running hook commands and explain what local files, memory, or session data each hook may access.

remediation.issue: Shared swarm memory may hold sensitive project context
remediation.suggestion: Warn users not to store secrets, credentials, or customer data in shared swarm memory.

content.value_statement: Complex AI development work needs coordination across specialized agents. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through agentic-flow swarm topologies, task routing, memory sharing, and hooks.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to initialize mesh, hierarchical, and adaptive swarm topologies.
Provides agentic-flow hook commands for setup, agent spawning, task orchestration, and session restore.
Outlines parallel, pipeline, and adaptive task execution patterns.
Demonstrates shared memory storage and retrieval for agent coordination.
Covers load balancing, fault tolerance, metrics, and hook-based synchronization.
limitations: Requires agentic-flow v1.5.11 or later and Node.js 18 or later.
Examples assume a configured swarm API or CLI is available.
Does not validate package provenance, credentials, or local hook side effects.
Large swarms can increase cost, latency, and coordination overhead.

use_cases.title: Coordinate API Delivery
use_cases.description: Plan coder, tester, reviewer, and architect agents for a backend feature with parallel tasks and review stages.

use_cases.title: Design Reliable Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Choose a mesh, hierarchical, or adaptive topology based on workload size, dependencies, and failure tolerance.

use_cases.title: Run Parallel Quality Work
use_cases.description: Split implementation, test writing, review, and metrics checks across specialized agents with shared context.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Small Swarm
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one feature task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a three-agent mesh swarm for a REST API feature with coding, testing, and review responsibilities.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Parallel Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate task splitting for faster delivery.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a parallel swarm workflow for this project goal. Include agent roles, dependencies, shared memory needs, and success checks.

prompt_templates.title: Select a Topology
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare mesh, hierarchical, and adaptive swarm topologies for this task. Recommend one and explain coordination risks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Swarm Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this swarm orchestration plan for package execution risk, shared memory exposure, task dependencies, and failure recovery gaps.

output_examples.input: Plan a swarm for adding a billing API.
output: Recommended topology: hierarchical, with an architect coordinator and specialist implementation agents.
Suggested agents: backend coder, database designer, tester, and reviewer.
Shared memory should include endpoint contracts, data model notes, and test status only.

output_examples.input: Review my agentic-flow hook plan before execution.
output: Pin the CLI package version before running npx commands.
Confirm which hooks read or write workspace state.
Exclude secrets and customer records from swarm memory.

output_examples.input: Choose a topology for a mixed frontend and backend project.
output_examples.output: Use adaptive topology when task complexity changes often. Start with clear agent roles, shared context boundaries, and timeout limits.

best_practices: Start with two or three agents before increasing swarm size.
Pin and review any CLI package before running hook commands.
Use shared memory only for necessary project context.
anti_patterns: Running unpinned npx commands in production workspaces.
Adding many agents before defining task boundaries.
Storing secrets or customer data in shared swarm memory.

faq.question: What does this skill help coordinate?
faq.answer: It helps coordinate multi-agent development workflows using agentic-flow topologies, shared memory, task orchestration, and hooks.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: The skill documents npx commands, but users should review and approve command execution in their own environment.

faq.question: What should I install first?
faq.answer: Install Node.js 18 or later and a reviewed agentic-flow version that meets the skill prerequisite.

faq.question: Can I use it for small tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. Start with two or three agents and expand only when coordination benefits outweigh overhead.

faq.question: What data should stay out of swarm memory?
faq.answer: Keep secrets, access tokens, customer data, and regulated records out of shared swarm memory.
